title: Weak relative Noether normalization
statement: Let $R$ and $A$ be commutative rings and let $h:\operatorname{Spec}(A)\to\operatorname{Spec}(R)$ be the induced morphism of affine schemes [def-pc-scheme]. Assume that $h$ is of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Let $N\ge0$ be an integer and suppose every scheme-theoretic fibre [def-pc-scheme-fibre] of $h$ has topological Krull dimension [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension] at most $N$. Then there exist an integer $d$ with $0\le d\le N$ and an $R$-algebra homomorphism $R[T_1,\ldots,T_d]\to A$ such that the induced morphism $\operatorname{Spec}(A)\to\operatorname{Spec}(R[T_1,\ldots,T_d])$ is quasi-finite (of finite type with finite discrete fibres, [pqf-def-quasifinite]).

source.place: More on Morphisms, Lemma Tag 0GTG (lemma-weak-relative-noether-normalization): a finite type ring map with fibre dimensions bounded by d admits a quasi-finite map from a polynomial ring in d variables over the base.
